_comment: Nightly benchmark P99 ceilings (nanoseconds). Keys under .metrics MUST match the metric label passed to row_pct() in benchmark/bench_*.cpp. CI's scripts/check-bench.sh parses bench stdout, picks the host-specific block under .hosts (or falls back to .metrics if the running host is not pinned), and fails the build when measured P99 exceeds the ceiling.
_jitter_policy: Multiplier applied to the measured P99 baseline depends on absolute scale. Sub-100ns hot paths (Property::set, set_any) get x3.0 because a single scheduler hiccup or icache miss is a meaningful fraction of the budget. Mid-range 100ns-1us paths get x2.0. Heavy ops above 1us get x1.5 since absolute jitter is a smaller share. The goal is a noise-tolerant ceiling that still catches a real 30-50% regression.
_host_keys: Host detection (lowercased OS-arch): 'macos-arm64', 'macos-x86_64', 'linux-x86_64', 'linux-aarch64', 'windows-x86_64', 'windows-aarch64'. Add a new key under .hosts when a CI runner with a materially different baseline comes online; until then the .metrics block is used as a generic fallback.

macos-arm64._baseline_note: Ceilings = quiet-host P99 × ._jitter_policy multiplier. Captured 2026-06-09 on an idle M-series host (no other heavy processes). On a busy developer machine these numbers will trip — that is intentional: a noisy machine should not anchor the regression budget. Use `scripts/check-bench.sh --runs 5` to take best-of-N and cancel local jitter, or run on a CI-grade quiet host.
